delete_library_entry.description: Take a title off the connected account's shelf. This takes the entry's own id rather than a title, on purpose: it is the one action here that destroys something, and an id that came out of a library listing or out of the action that wrote it cannot be a title that resolved to the wrong show. The entry is read before it is removed, so the step reports what it took off and an id belonging to somebody else's library is named rather than relayed as a bare refusal. Needs the Kitsu account on this connection: install it with an email and a password.

search_manga.description: Search Kitsu's manga catalogue by text and by category. Each result comes back with its titles in every language Kitsu holds, its score as a number you can compare, its chapter and volume counts, the magazine it ran in, and its pages on MyAnimeList and AniList. No Kitsu account needed.

set_library_entry.description: Put a title on the connected account's shelf, or change where it sits: its status, how far through it you are, a score out of ten, a private note. Kitsu has no upsert and refuses a second entry for a title already in the library, so this looks first and then either creates or updates, and says which it did. Every field left blank is left alone on an entry that already existed, and a new entry with no status given starts as watching or reading now. Needs the Kitsu account on this connection: install it with an email and a password.

description: Search Kitsu's anime and manga catalogue and read or change a Kitsu library. Look a title up by name and get its synopsis, its score as a number you can compare, its categories, its episodes or chapters, its characters, what it is a sequel to and where it streams, with everything Kitsu returns as a bare link already resolved. Read anybody's public library to see what they are watching and how far through they are. Add an account to the connection and you can also change your own: put a title on a shelf, record progress, score it out of ten and take it off again. The catalogue needs no account at all, and nor does reading somebody else's public library; only changing a library, and reading your own, do.
